newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Product Swaps - Gas oil up on physical cover.
newsitem.headline: Asia Product Swaps - Gas oil up on physical cover.

text.p: Singapore gas oil swaps rose at midday on Friday as players entered the market to hedge their earlier record physical sales, brokers said.
"The buyers came in late last night and today to cover their physical sales," one broker said.
May gas oil swaps were last quoted at $25.95/$26.10 per barrel, up from Thursday's $25.50/$25.55, brokers said.
May traded this morning at $25.95, they said.
June swaps also rose in tandem and was quoted at $24.85/$25.00, up from Thursday's $24.35/$24.55, brokers said.
Traders said the higher prices were inevitable given the record 2.44 million barrels of physical gas oil traded late on Thursday.

The sellers of these cargoes were quickly seen in the swaps market seeking to hedge their fixed prices sales at between $25.70 to $26.60 per barrel free-on-board Singapore for cargoes loading in from mid to second half of May.
The physical purchase on Thursday took the tally of gas oil purchased by the group of three traders to more than 17 million barrels since the buying spree started on March 3.
The jet fuel/gas oil spread (regrade) was steady on sustained support from traders who on Thursday bought one physical jet fuel cargo at $24.25 per barrel, traders said.
May regrade was last quoted at minus 50/30 cents while June was seen at 60/75 cents, brokers said.
Traders said jet fuel purchases by the local traders which totalled about three million barrels since March 3 has given the market a much needed boost in a period of low demand.
The fuel oil swaps were steady with May last quoted at $97.50/$98.50 per tonne.
